title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Hydrostatic pressure at depth h in a liquid of density ρ?
cards.a:
Total Pressure: P = P₀ + ρ g h, where P₀ is atmospheric pressure.
Gauge Pressure: P_gauge = P - P₀ = ρ g h.
cards.hint: Pressure is isotropic (same in all directions at a given depth) and independent of the cross-sectional shape of the container.

cards.q: State Pascal's Law and its primary hydraulic application formula.
cards.a:
Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of fluid and walls of vessel.
Hydraulic lift formula: F₁ / A₁ = F₂ / A₂ ⇒ F₂ = F₁ · (A₂ / A₁).
cards.hint: Force is multiplied by the ratio of piston areas A₂/A₁.

cards.q: What is Surface Tension (T) and Surface Energy?
cards.a:
Surface Tension: Tangential force per unit length acting perpendicular to an imaginary line on the liquid surface (T = F / L). SI unit: N/m or J/m², dimensions: [M¹ L⁰ T⁻²].
Surface Energy: Potential energy per unit area of surface film (E = T · ΔA).
cards.hint: Work done in stretching a liquid surface by area ΔA is W = T · ΔA.

cards.q: Work done in blowing a liquid drop vs a soap bubble of radius r?
cards.a:
Liquid drop (1 free surface): W = 4 π r² T
Soap bubble (2 free surfaces): W = 2 × (4 π r² T) = 8 π r² T.
cards.hint: Major student trap: Soap bubble has BOTH inside and outside air surfaces, so multiply area by 2!

cards.q: A big drop of radius R breaks into n identical droplets: Work done and temperature change?
cards.a:
Radius of small droplet: r = R / n^(1/3)
Increase in surface area: ΔA = 4 π R² (n^(1/3) - 1)
Work done / energy absorbed: W = 4 π R² T (n^(1/3) - 1).
Temperature DECREASES (liquid cools).
cards.hint: Surface area increases, so energy is absorbed from internal heat, causing cooling!

cards.q: What is Angle of Contact θ? Give values for water-glass and mercury-glass.
cards.a:
Angle between tangent to liquid surface and solid surface inside the liquid.
Pure water & clean glass: θ ≈ 0° (concave meniscus, wets glass).
Mercury & glass: θ ≈ 140° (obtuse, convex meniscus, does not wet glass).
cards.hint: If θ < 90° (acute), liquid rises in capillary; if θ > 90° (obtuse), liquid is depressed.

cards.q: Excess pressure (Laplace's formula) for liquid drop, soap bubble, and air bubble in liquid?
cards.a:
Liquid drop in air: ΔP = 2 T / r
Air bubble in liquid: ΔP = 2 T / r
Soap bubble in air: ΔP = 4 T / r (due to 2 free surfaces).
cards.hint: Smaller bubbles have larger excess pressure (ΔP ∝ 1/r). Air flows from smaller bubble to larger bubble!

cards.q: Capillary rise formula (Ascent formula / Jurin's Law)?
cards.a: h = (2 T cos θ) / (r ρ g), where r is capillary tube radius, ρ is liquid density, and θ is angle of contact.
cards.hint: Notice h ∝ 1/r (thinner bore produces higher rise).

cards.q: What happens if a capillary tube has insufficient length L < h?
cards.a: The liquid does NOT overflow. It reaches the top rim and increases its radius of curvature R' such that h · r = L · R' (or R' cos θ' = r).
cards.hint: Liquid adjusts its meniscus curvature to maintain equilibrium without overflowing!

cards.q: Effect of temperature and impurities on Surface Tension?
cards.a:
Temperature: Surface tension DECREASES with rise in temperature (becomes zero at critical temperature).
Impurities: Highly soluble impurities (NaCl) INCREASE surface tension; sparingly soluble (phenol/soap/detergent) DECREASE it.
cards.hint: Detergents lower surface tension, allowing water to penetrate cloth fibers easily.

cards.q: Newton's formula for Viscous Force and coefficient of viscosity η?
cards.a:
F = - η A (dv / dx), where A is contact area and dv/dx is velocity gradient.
SI unit of η: N·s/m² (Pa·s) or kg/(m·s). CGS unit: poise (1 Pa·s = 10 poise). Dimensions: [M¹ L⁻¹ T⁻¹].
cards.hint: Negative sign indicates viscous force opposes relative motion between fluid layers.

cards.q: State Stokes' Law for viscous drag on a spherical body.
cards.a: F_v = 6 π η r v, where r is sphere radius, v is velocity, and η is viscosity of medium.
cards.hint: Valid strictly for laminar flow past small, smooth, spherical bodies in infinite medium.

cards.q: Formula for Terminal Velocity v_t of a sphere falling through a viscous fluid?
cards.a: v_t = (2/9) · [ r² (ρ - σ) g ] / η, where ρ is sphere density and σ is fluid density.
cards.hint: Key MHT-CET proportionality: v_t ∝ r² (terminal velocity is proportional to the square of radius!).

cards.q: If 8 identical raindrops falling with terminal velocity v coalesce into a single drop, what is the new terminal velocity?
cards.a:
New velocity v' = 4 v.
Since volume is conserved: (4/3)π R³ = 8 × (4/3)π r³ ⇒ R = 2 r. Terminal velocity v_t ∝ r² ⇒ v' = (2)² v = 4 v.
cards.hint: General formula for n coalescing droplets: v' = n^(2/3) · v.

cards.q: Reynolds Number R_e: Formula and flow classification?
cards.a:
R_e = ρ v d / η, where d is pipe diameter.
1. R_e < 1000: Streamline (laminar) flow.
2. 1000 < R_e < 2000: Unstable flow.
3. R_e > 2000: Turbulent flow.
cards.hint: Dimensionless pure number [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰] characterizing fluid flow turbulence.

cards.q: State the Equation of Continuity for steady streamline flow.
cards.a:
A₁ v₁ = A₂ v₂ = constant (or A · v = volume flow rate dV/dt).
Mass flow rate: ρ A v = constant.
cards.hint: Based on Conservation of MASS for an incompressible, non-viscous fluid.

cards.q: State Bernoulli's Principle and its equation.
cards.a:
P + (1/2) ρ v² + ρ g h = constant.
Pressure Energy per unit volume + Kinetic Energy per unit volume + Potential Energy per unit volume = constant.
cards.hint: Based on the Law of Conservation of ENERGY for ideal fluid streamline flow.

cards.q: Torricelli's Law: Velocity of efflux from an orifice at depth h below open liquid surface?
cards.hint: Identical to the velocity acquired by a freely falling body through height h!

cards.q: Aerodynamic lift on an airplane wing and spinning ball (Magnus Effect): Bernoulli explanation?
cards.a: Air moves faster over upper curved wing (v_top > v_bottom). By Bernoulli's equation, pressure above is lower (P_top < P_bottom), producing upward dynamic lift.
cards.hint: High speed corresponds to low pressure; low speed corresponds to high pressure.

cards.q: Venturimeter formula for volume rate of flow Q?
cards.a: Q = A₁ A₂ √[ (2 h ρ_m g) / [ ρ (A₁² - A₂²) ] ], where h is manometer height difference.
cards.hint: Direct application of Bernoulli's theorem to measure fluid flow speed in pipes.

cards.q: Effect of temperature on viscosity of liquids vs gases?
cards.a:
Liquids: Viscosity DECREASES with temperature (molecules move apart, cohesive forces weaken).
Gases: Viscosity INCREASES with temperature (molecular diffusion and collisions increase: η ∝ √T).
cards.hint: High-yield conceptual trap! Liquids get thinner, while gases get more viscous on heating.

cards.q: Critical velocity v_c of fluid flow in a tube of diameter d?
cards.hint: Maximum velocity up to which flow remains streamline.

cards.q: Two soap bubbles of radii r₁ and r₂ touch. What is the radius of common interface r?
cards.a: r = (r₁ · r₂) / (r₁ - r₂)  (assuming r₁ > r₂).
cards.hint: ΔP = ΔP₂ - ΔP₁ ⇒ 4T/r = 4T/r₂ - 4T/r₁ ⇒ 1/r = 1/r₂ - 1/r₁.

cards.q: Pressure, Velocity, and Height heads in Bernoulli's equation?
cards.a:
Divide Bernoulli equation by ρ g:
P / (ρ g) [Pressure Head] + v² / (2 g) [Velocity Head] + h [Gravitational Head] = constant.
cards.hint: Each term has dimensions of length [L¹] and is expressed in metres of fluid column.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: Can gauge pressure ever be negative?
cards.a: YES. Gauge pressure P - P₀ is negative whenever absolute pressure P is less than atmospheric pressure P₀ (vacuum/suction).
cards.hint: Absolute pressure P can never be negative, but gauge pressure certainly can!
